architecture.title: Alto Ops Claw, hardened — what can leave the sandbox
architecture.caption: The production policy (research tutorial Lab 6.1) leaves three ways out of the sandbox: the BMS over MCP (read tools only, write tools denied), the on-prem OTel collector (POST /v1/traces only) and inference.local, which the supervisor intercepts and the gateway routes to the local model. Everything else — provider hosts, package registries, cloud metadata — is denied by default or always blocked. Writes go through the human-approved approvals service, which the claw can only ask (the exercise).

sequence.title: A prompt-injected write, and the path a real write takes
sequence.caption: A booby-trapped tool result tells the agent to change a setpoint. The MCP tools/call for write_setpoint hits a deny_rule and gets a 403 before it reaches the BMS (lab 07-2 shows the course gate doing the same against the real mock server). The legitimate path is a ticket to the approvals service: the claw can create and read it, a human approves it outside the sandbox.

charts.title: Twelve attacker steps — how many worked
charts.caption: From lab 07-1, run on this Mac with the course's policykit teaching model (not OpenShell). The two steps that still work under prod are a read and a write inside /sandbox; prod leaves them no host to send data to.

charts.title: Twelve weakened policies — which checker notices
charts.caption: From lab 07-2 on this Mac. The parser catches field names (Version, an mcp typo); validate catches values (root, Version); only the lint sees the quiet weakenings that parse fine — audit, L4, access: full, wildcards, provider hosts, extra binaries, /usr, best_effort, tls: skip. One copy (Version) is caught by two checkers.

charts.title: Eleven broken blueprints — the rule that caught each
charts.caption: From lab 07-3 on this Mac: the course validator applies the rules the research tutorial lists for an external-gateway blueprint.yaml. The real checks run in nemoclaw-blueprint-runner on the Spark.
